question: Does an executive clarification regarding seniority operate retrospectively?
claim_sentence: An executive clarification regarding seniority that specifies it applies henceforth does not operate retrospectively.

supporting_passages.case_title: UNION OF INDIA & ORS. versus K. VELUSAMY & ORS.
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: The clarification issued vide GO dated 04.08.2015 does not operate retrospectively as it is specifically provided in the said GO that 'henceforth', the seniority in respect of Industrial Establishments will be governed by the relevant clause of OM dated 04.11.1992 – It is trite law that executive instructions cannot have retrospective effect unless expressly provided.

question: Can a judicial authority be impleaded in an appeal against its own order?
claim_sentence: A judicial or quasi-judicial authority must not be impleaded in an appeal against its order issued solely in exercise of its adjudicatory function.

supporting_passages.case_title: STATE OF RAJASTHAN versus CHHITAR & ANR.
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: An authority (either a judicial or quasi-judicial authority) must not be impleaded in an appeal against its order if the order was issued solely in exercise of its 'adjudicatory function'. [Para 33 (a)] Judicial Authority or quasi-judicial Authority – Whether an Authority could be impleaded as a party respondent in a proceeding where its order is challenged – Held: No.

question: Does a party's status as a statutory undertaking alter the legal standards governing arbitration proceedings?
claim_sentence: The law governing arbitration proceedings cannot be applied differently merely because a party is a statutory undertaking.

supporting_passages.case_title: NATIONAL HIGHWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA versus M/S SANGAM ENTERPRISES
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: Law qua arbitration proceedings, cannot be any different merely because of the status of the respondent as a statutory undertaking – High Court ought not to have based its decision on the condition for the grant of stay on the status of the respondent as a statutory authority – Commercial disputes must be decided on legal principles applicable uniformly.

question: Can the period to deposit the balance sale consideration in an auction sale be extended without party consent?
claim_sentence: The period to deposit the balance sale consideration in an auction sale is freely extendable without the written consent of the parties.

supporting_passages.case_title: RAMESHWAR DASS versus M/S OM PARKASH BAL KISHAN
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: The period to deposit the balance sale consideration under r.9(4) is not absolute/sacrosanct and is extendable with the consent in writing of the parties – r.9(4) will only come into play when there is default on part of the party i.e. the auction purchaser to deposit the balance amount – In the absence of written consent, extension cannot be granted unilaterally.

question: Who is entitled to make an application under Order XXI Rule 99 CPC complaining of dispossession?
claim_sentence: Under Order XXI Rule 99 CPC, an application complaining of dispossession can be made by the judgment debtor.

supporting_passages.case_title: PRADEEP KUMAR versus THE STATE OF U.P.
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: Yes – Under Or.XXI, r.99, where any person other than the judgment debtor is dispossessed of immovable property by the holder of a decree for the possession of such property, or where such property has been sold in execution of a decree, by the purchaser thereof, he may make an application to the Court complaining of such dispossession.

question: Can a dissenting financial creditor challenge a resolution plan if the plan is compliant with law?
claim_sentence: A dissenting financial creditor may challenge any approved resolution plan even when the plan is non-discriminatory and conforms to law.

supporting_passages.case_title: DBS BANK LTD. versus SHAILENDRA AJMERA & ANR.
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: s.30(2)(b)(ii) forfends the dissenting financial creditor from settling for a lower amount payable under the resolution plan – A financial creditor can dissent if the resolution plan is discriminatory or against a provision of law – However, a dissenting financial creditor cannot challenge commercial wisdom of CoC if the plan is legally compliant.

question: What is the statutory duration of paid maternity leave under the Maternity Benefit Act?
claim_sentence: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, female employees are entitled to twenty-six weeks of paid leave for the birth of a first child.

question: Are operational creditors entitled to priority payment before financial debts can be restructured?
claim_sentence: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, operational creditors must be paid in full before financial debt can be restructured.

supporting_passages.case_title: SUNDER LAL versus STATE OF HARYANA
supporting_passages.passage_text: Held: During the pendency of the petitions, it appears that some settlement has been arrived at between the complainants and the 13 accused – The subsequent purchasers (of the premises in question) have paid an amount of Rs. 10 lacs to each of the tenants, and in lieu thereof tenants have vacated.

question: What is the statutory desertion period required for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ib)?
claim_sentence: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, desertion for a continuous period of not less than two years is a statutory ground for divorce.

question: Must a judicial authority be impleaded as a party respondent in an appeal against its order?
claim_sentence: A judicial or quasi-judicial authority must always be impleaded as a necessary party respondent in an appeal against its adjudicatory order.

question: Did the Supreme Court hold that executive seniority instructions apply retrospectively?
claim_sentence: The Supreme Court held that the executive clarification on seniority operates retrospectively to alter past promotions.

claim_sentence: The Supreme Court held that statutory authorities are subject to a separate and relaxed standard under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
